issues.description: The problem statement requires marking the end of the main loop with the label `loop_end`, but the template does not contain this label and the solution uses a different label name (`end_loop`). This cross-artifact naming mismatch (problem vs. solution, and template missing the label) can confuse students about the exact label they must add and where to place it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the label name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the solution label `end_loop` to `loop_end`, and/or add the `loop_end` label at the end of the main section in the template so it matches the problem statement. Alternatively, update the problem statement to reference `end_loop` if that name is preferred.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to mark the end of the main loop with the label `loop_end` (problem_statement.md line 22), but the provided solution uses the label `end_loop` (helloWorld.asm line 17). The template also does not contain the requested `loop_end` label. This mismatch between `loop_end` and `end_loop` is an unintended naming inconsistency that can confuse students trying to map the assignment instruction to the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the label in the solution from `end_loop` to `loop_end` (or update the problem statement to request `end_loop`) so the label name is consistent across problem statement, template, and solution. For example, change `end_loop:` to `loop_end:` in helloWorld.asm.
